strategy_title: Increasing BLOCK_K Worsens Shared Memory Bottleneck
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_K (e.g. from 32 to 64-128) in Triton GEMM autotune configs to reduce register pressure can backfire: larger BLOCK_K tiles require proportionally more shared memory per block, which reduces the Block Limit Shared Mem from 3 to 1 block/SM, cutting theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 6.25% and worsening scheduler stalls (no-eligible-warp rate rose from 51.8% to 78.2%). Simultaneously, the larger shared memory tiles amplified shared memory bank conflicts from 5.4-way to 12-way (uncoalesced wavefronts rose from 56% to 76%), making the memory bottleneck significantly worse. When the kernel already has severe shared memory bank conflicts, increasing tile sizes that expand shared memory usage will compound the problem rather than solve it.
fast_pseudocode:
# After (WORSE): BLOCK_K=64-128, larger shared mem, 128 regs/thread, 6.25% occupancy
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    Config({'BLOCK_M':64,'BLOCK_N':64,'BLOCK_K':64},   num_stages=5, num_warps=4),
    Config({'BLOCK_M':128,'BLOCK_N':128,'BLOCK_K':128}, num_stages=3, num_warps=4),
    # ... all BLOCK_K=64 or BLOCK_K=128
])
# Result: Block Limit Shared Mem dropped to 1, occupancy halved, bank conflicts doubled
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern. Increasing BLOCK_K to reduce register pressure is counterproductive when shared memory bank conflicts are already severe (>5-way) and shared memory is already a binding occupancy limiter.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_K when: (1) shared memory bank conflicts are already high (>5-way), (2) Block Limit Shared Mem is already <=3, (3) the kernel's shared memory access pattern has structural stride issues that will worsen with larger tiles. Instead, fix the bank conflict pattern first (e.g. padding shared memory arrays) before increasing tile sizes.
framework_notes: Triton: num_stages controls software pipeline depth and directly multiplies shared memory usage (each stage requires one tile buffer). Increasing both BLOCK_K and num_stages simultaneously can cause shared memory to become the binding occupancy limiter even when registers were the previous bottleneck. Check Block Limit Shared Mem in NCU Occupancy section before increasing tile sizes.

strategy_title: Reducing BLOCK_K + num_stages Worsens L1 Saturation Despite Better Occupancy
strategy_description: Switching Triton GEMM autotune configs to BLOCK_K=32 with num_stages=2/3 reduced dynamic shared memory per block from 65 KB to 16 KB and improved theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 25% (Block Limit Registers rose from 2 to 4). However, the increased block count (grid 512→2048, waves 1.94→3.88) caused L1/TEX cache throughput to saturate at 96.8% (up from 64.1%), Mem Busy to rise to 93.8%, and warp cycles per issued instruction to jump from 4.1 to 15.6 cycles — indicating severe L1 cache contention from the higher concurrency. The net result was a 1.8× slowdown (7.2 ms → 13.1 ms): more occupancy does not help when the memory subsystem becomes the new binding bottleneck due to increased concurrent tile traffic. When the baseline kernel already has severe shared memory bank conflicts (5.4-way) and uncoalesced accesses (56% excess wavefronts), reducing tile size increases the number of tiles and amplifies L1 pressure rather than relieving it.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (baseline, 7.2 ms): BLOCK_K=32, num_stages=3/4, 65 KB smem/block
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    Config({'BLOCK_M':128,'BLOCK_N':128,'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=3, num_warps=4),
    Config({'BLOCK_M':256,'BLOCK_N':128,'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=3, num_warps=8),
    Config({'BLOCK_M':64, 'BLOCK_N':256,'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=4, num_warps=4),
    # ... all BLOCK_K=32, num_stages=3-5
])
# Result: 12.5% occupancy, 4.1 cycles/inst, L1 64%, Mem Busy 60.8%
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed, 13.1 ms): BLOCK_K=32, num_stages=2/3, 16 KB smem/block
@triton.autotune(configs=[
    Config({'BLOCK_M':64, 'BLOCK_N':64, 'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=2, num_warps=4),
    Config({'BLOCK_M':128,'BLOCK_N':128,'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=2, num_warps=4),
    Config({'BLOCK_M':256,'BLOCK_N':128,'BLOCK_K':32}, num_stages=2, num_warps=8),
    # ... all BLOCK_K=32, num_stages=2/3
])
# Result: 25% occupancy, 15.6 cycles/inst, L1 96.8%, Mem Busy 93.8%
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern. Reducing num_stages to lower shared memory per block while keeping BLOCK_K=32 increases concurrent block count and saturates L1/TEX cache when the kernel already has structural shared memory bank conflicts.
do_not_apply_when: Do not reduce num_stages to 2 when the kernel already has severe shared memory bank conflicts (>5-way) and uncoalesced shared accesses (>50% excess wavefronts). The increased block concurrency from lower smem/block will saturate L1/TEX (>90% Mem Busy) and cause warp stall cycles to multiply (4→15 cycles/inst), negating any occupancy gain. The root cause (bank conflicts from strided shared memory access pattern) must be fixed first — e.g. via shared memory padding or TMA-based access — before tuning occupancy via num_stages.
framework_notes: Triton on Hopper (H200): Triton's software pipeline allocates (BLOCK_M + BLOCK_N) * BLOCK_K * num_stages * element_size bytes of shared memory. Reducing num_stages from 3→2 cuts smem from 65 KB to 16 KB per block, allowing 4 blocks/SM instead of 2. But if the access pattern has structural bank conflicts (stride-K loads across shared memory banks), more concurrent blocks amplify total bank conflict traffic proportionally. The eviction_policy='evict_first' hint was also removed in this iteration, which may have contributed to L1 saturation. CUDA equivalent: reducing __shared__ buffer depth in a manually pipelined GEMM has the same trade-off.

strategy_title: tl.make_block_ptr TMA Loads Worsen Bank Conflicts on This Kernel
strategy_description: Replacing raw pointer arithmetic loads with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.advance in a Triton GEMM kernel (intended to trigger TMA swizzled shared memory layout on Hopper) actually worsened shared memory bank conflicts from 5.3-way to 12-way and increased uncoalesced shared wavefronts from 56% to 76%. The L1/TEX hit rate collapsed from 64.1% to 0.02%, L1/TEX throughput saturated at 94.8%, Mem Busy rose from 62.8% to 91.5%, and warp cycles per issued instruction jumped from 4.1 to 11.6 — all indicating the block pointer path did not engage TMA swizzling as expected, and instead increased memory pressure by changing the tile configuration (smaller smem/block, more concurrent blocks, grid 512→2048). The autotune config changes that accompanied the block pointer switch (adding smaller BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N configs, changing num_stages) likely selected a config with more concurrent blocks that amplified L1 contention, masking or preventing any TMA benefit.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (7.1 ms): raw pointer arithmetic, BLOCK_K=32, 32 KB smem/block
X_ptrs = X_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_xm + rk[None, :] * stride_xk
W_ptrs = W_ptr + offs_n[None, :] * stride_wn + rk[:, None] * stride_wk
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    x = tl.load(X_ptrs, mask=x_mask, other=0.0)
    w = tl.load(W_ptrs, mask=w_mask, other=0.0)
    acc = tl.dot(x, w, acc, allow_tf32=False)
    X_ptrs += BLOCK_K * stride_xk
    W_ptrs += BLOCK_K * stride_wk
# Result: 5.3-way bank conflicts, 56% excess wavefronts, L1 hit 64%, Mem Busy 62.8%
fast_pseudocode:
# AFTER (13.4 ms, WORSE): block pointer loads, 16 KB smem/block, grid 2048
X_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=X_ptr, shape=(M,K), strides=(stride_xm,stride_xk),
    offsets=(pid_m*BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M,BLOCK_K), order=(1,0))
W_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(base=W_ptr, shape=(K,N), strides=(stride_wk,stride_wn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n*BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K,BLOCK_N), order=(0,1))
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    x = tl.load(X_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    w = tl.load(W_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    acc = tl.dot(x, w, acc, allow_tf32=False)
    X_block_ptr = tl.advance(X_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    W_block_ptr = tl.advance(W_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
# Result: 12-way bank conflicts, 76% excess wavefronts, L1 hit 0.02%, Mem Busy 91.5%
applicable_when: Never apply this specific pattern in isolation. tl.make_block_ptr alone does not guarantee TMA swizzled layout or bank-conflict elimination; the autotune config selection (tile sizes, num_stages) must also be controlled to avoid increasing concurrent block count and L1 pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Do not switch from raw pointer arithmetic to tl.make_block_ptr when: (1) the kernel already has structural shared memory bank conflicts (>5-way) that are not caused by the pointer style alone, (2) the autotune config space is simultaneously changed to include smaller tiles that increase grid size and concurrent block count, (3) L1/TEX is already under moderate pressure (>60% throughput) — adding more concurrent blocks will saturate it. The block pointer change must be isolated from config changes to determine its true effect. Also do not apply when the kernel's shared memory access pattern has stride issues that tl.make_block_ptr does not fix (e.g. non-power-of-two strides or layouts incompatible with TMA swizzling).
framework_notes: Triton on Hopper (H200): tl.make_block_ptr is intended to enable TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) hardware with swizzled shared memory layout, but this requires the Triton compiler to successfully lower the block pointer to TMA instructions. If the tile shape, stride, or order parameters are not compatible with TMA constraints, Triton may fall back to a non-swizzled path that is no better (or worse) than raw pointer loads. The simultaneous autotune config change (adding 64x64 and other small-tile configs) caused the autotuner to select a config with 16 KB smem/block (vs 32 KB before), quadrupling the grid size (512→2048) and amplifying L1 contention. These two changes (block ptr + config) were conflated, making it impossible to attribute the regression to either alone.

strategy_title: Fix W Block Ptr Order + tf32x3 Reduces Registers and Improves Occupancy
strategy_description: In a Triton GEMM kernel already using tl.make_block_ptr and input_precision='tf32x3', correcting the W matrix block pointer layout from shape=(N,K)/order=(1,0) with tl.trans() to shape=(K,N)/order=(1,0) without tl.trans() reduced registers per thread from 255 to 142, allowing Block Limit Registers to rise from 2 to 3 blocks/SM and theoretical occupancy from 12.5% to 18.75%. This also reduced dynamic shared memory per block from 98 KB to 33 KB, enabling more concurrent blocks (grid 512→2048, waves 1.94→5.17), which improved compute SM throughput from 27.9% to 38.1% and reduced no-eligible-warp cycles from 76.9% to 60.8%. The net result was a 2.27× speedup (3.98 ms → 1.75 ms implied), demonstrating that the W block pointer memory layout (shape and order parameters) directly affects register allocation and occupancy even when tf32x3 Tensor Cores are already active.
slow_pseudocode:
# W loaded as (N,K) tile then transposed — high register pressure, 98 KB smem/block
W_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=W_ptr, shape=(N, K), strides=(stride_wn, stride_wk),
    offsets=(pid_n * BLOCK_N, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K), order=(1, 0)
)
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    w = tl.load(W_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    acc = tl.dot(x, tl.trans(w), acc, input_precision='tf32x3')  # tl.trans() needed
    W_block_ptr = tl.advance(W_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
# Result: 255 regs/thread, 98 KB smem/block, 12.5% occupancy, 3.98 ms
fast_pseudocode:
# W loaded directly as (K,N) tile — lower register pressure, 33 KB smem/block
W_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=W_ptr, shape=(K, N), strides=(stride_wk, stride_wn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n * BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N), order=(1, 0)
)
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    w = tl.load(W_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    acc = tl.dot(x, w, acc, input_precision='tf32x3')  # no tl.trans() needed
    W_block_ptr = tl.advance(W_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
# Result: 142 regs/thread, 33 KB smem/block, 18.75% occupancy, 1.75 ms
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel on Hopper (sm_90) already using tl.make_block_ptr + input_precision='tf32x3', where W is stored as (N,K) but loaded as (N,BLOCK_K) tiles and then transposed via tl.trans() before tl.dot(). If registers_per_thread is near 255 and Block Limit Registers is 2, the tl.trans() call is consuming significant register budget. Reshaping the W block pointer to load (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N) tiles directly eliminates the transpose and reduces register pressure.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply when W is not stored in a layout compatible with direct (K,N) block pointer access (e.g. non-contiguous strides). Do not apply if the autotune config space simultaneously changes tile sizes in a way that increases shared memory per block beyond the per-SM budget. Note that this change increases grid size (more blocks), which can amplify L1 contention if the kernel is already L1-saturated (>90% L1/TEX throughput).
framework_notes: Triton on Hopper (H200): tl.trans() on a loaded tile is not free — it forces the compiler to materialize the transposed layout in registers, consuming significant register budget. When W is stored as row-major (N,K) with stride_wn=K, stride_wk=1, it can equivalently be described as (K,N) with stride_wk=1, stride_wn=K, allowing direct (BLOCK_K,BLOCK_N) tile loads without tl.trans(). The order=(1,0) parameter on the W block pointer (N-dim fastest-varying) is critical for TMA swizzle compatibility on Hopper. The SharedMemoryConflicts rule disappeared after this fix, confirming the order parameter was the root cause of the 5.5-way bank conflicts seen in the 'after' profiling of iteration 3.

strategy_title: Switch tf32x3 to tf32 to Eliminate Register Spill
strategy_description: Changing tl.dot input_precision from 'tf32x3' (3-pass Ozaki splitting) to 'tf32' (single-pass) was predicted to eliminate register spill caused by 255 registers/thread, but the profiling data shows no change in any NCU metric: registers/thread remained at 255, occupancy stayed at 12.5%, MemoryCacheAccessPattern local load/store rules persisted at ~52.5% estimated speedup, and duration was essentially unchanged (3.98 ms → 4.0 ms). Despite the reported 1.8x speedup, the NCU profiles are nearly identical, suggesting the speedup came from a different source (e.g. autotuner re-selection, measurement noise, or a non-kernel-level change) rather than the tf32x3→tf32 precision change itself. The tf32x3→tf32 change alone did not reduce register pressure or eliminate local memory spill on this kernel.
slow_pseudocode:
# tf32x3: 3-pass Ozaki splitting, 255 regs/thread, register spill to L2
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    x = tl.load(X_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    w = tl.load(W_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    acc = tl.dot(x, tl.trans(w), acc, input_precision='tf32x3')
    X_block_ptr = tl.advance(X_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    W_block_ptr = tl.advance(W_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
fast_pseudocode:
# tf32: single-pass, same 255 regs/thread, same register spill
for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    x = tl.load(X_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    w = tl.load(W_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0,1), padding_option='zero')
    acc = tl.dot(x, tl.trans(w), acc, input_precision='tf32')
    X_block_ptr = tl.advance(X_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    W_block_ptr = tl.advance(W_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
# NCU metrics unchanged: 255 regs, 12.5% occupancy, MemoryCacheAccessPattern still at 52.5%
applicable_when: Kernel uses input_precision='tf32x3' in tl.dot and registers/thread is at 255 with MemoryCacheAccessPattern local load/store rules triggered. Theory predicts tf32x3 triples register state for in-flight accumulation.
do_not_apply_when: NCU profiling shows registers/thread remains at 255 after the change (as observed here). If the MemoryCacheAccessPattern local load/store rules persist unchanged after switching to 'tf32', the register spill is not caused by the 3-pass splitting overhead but by some other structural property of the kernel (e.g. large accumulator tiles, complex epilogue). Do not expect this change to reduce register pressure when the compiler cannot lower the register count regardless of precision mode.
framework_notes: Triton on Hopper (H200): input_precision='tf32x3' implements Ozaki-style 3-pass FP32 decomposition for higher accuracy. The theory that this triples register pressure relative to 'tf32' did not hold in practice for this kernel — registers/thread stayed at 255 in both cases. The 1.8x speedup reported may reflect autotuner re-selection or measurement variance rather than the precision change. The MemoryCacheAccessPattern local load/store bottleneck (52.5% estimated speedup, 1/32 bytes/sector utilization) remains unresolved and is the dominant optimization target.
